This Appeal, Coming On For Admission, This Day,

 Judgment

This appeal is preferred by the appellant-claimant challenging the judgment and award dated 30.11.2019 passed in MVC No.435/2017 by Senior Civil Judge and Additional MACT, Kundapura (for short 'the tribunal').

entities.text: Senior Civil Judge and Additional MACT, Kundapura
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: This appeal is founded on the premise of inadequate and meager compensation awarded by the tribunal.
2. Parties to the appeal shall be referred to as per their status before the tribunal.

3. Brief facts of the case is as under:
The claimant was proceeding as a pillion rider in a motorbike bearing No.KA-19-Q-6268 along with rider on 24.10.2016.

When the motorbike reached near Belooru Hunsemakki road, Hombadi-Mandadi Village, Kundapura Taluk, a car bearing registration No.KA-20-MA-3728 driven by its NC: 2024:KHC:2210 driver came in a rash and negligent manner, so as to endanger human life and safety and dashed against the motorcycle, in which the claimant was proceeding as a pillion rider.
Due to the impact, the claimant sustained grievous injuries.

He was immediately taken to N.R. Acharya hospital, Koteshwara, where he was treated as an inpatient, incurred financial expenditures and due to the injuries suffered, he has encountered permanent disability.
3.1.

It is stated that the claimant was hale and healthy prior to the occurrence of the accident and by doing centering work and painting work, he was earning a sum of Rs.20,000/-
per month.

Due to the injuries sustained in the accident, he was unable to do his work, as he was able to do prior to the occurrence of the accident and thereby, he has encountered financial difficulties, mental and emotional trauma.

Hence, he has filed claim petition seeking compensation Sri Ananda vs Sri Manoj Kumar on 17 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/112474742/
2 against the respondents who are the owner and insurer of the offending vehicle.

entities.text: Sri Ananda vs Sri Manoj Kumar
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 3.2. The respondent No.1 was placed exparte and respondent No.2/insurance company has filed detailed NC: 2024:KHC:2210 statement of objections denying the entire claim made by the claimant including his age, avocation, income and negligence attributed against the driver of the car.
However, it admitted the policy in respect of offending vehicle.

However, it is stated that its liability is subject to the terms and conditions of the policy and that the respondent No.1 violated the terms and conditions of the policy and hence, sought for dismissal of the claim petition.
3.3. On the basis of pleading, the tribunal framed relevant issues for consideration.

3.4. In order to substantiate the issues and to prove the case, the claimant examined himself as PW.1 and also examined an orthopedic surgeon - Dr. Pradeep Kumar Shetty as PW.2 and got marked Exs.P1 to P50, whereas, the respondent produced and marked Ex.R1 and did not adduce any evidence.
3.5. Based on both oral and documentary evidence, the Tribunal awarded compensation of Rs.3,06,894/- along with interest @ 6% per annum from the date of petition.

The liability was fixed on respondent No.2/insurance company and it was NC: 2024:KHC:2210 directed to pay compensation of Rs.3,06,894/- from the date of award.
4.
It is the vehement contention of the learned counsel for the appellant that the tribunal has committed an error in not awarding reasonable compensation.

It has not assessed the proper income to award reasonable compensation, whereby, there is an error committed by the tribunal,
which is apparent on the face of the record.

It is also the contention of the learned counsel for the appellant that the tribunal has not taken into account, the evidence adduced by the doctor - PW.2 for assessment of disability and has assessed disability to an extent of 14% which requires to be enhanced.
It is also contended by the learned counsel for the appellant that under other heads also the tribunal has awarded meager compensation which calls for enhancement.

He further contended that though, the doctor - PW.2 has stated that the claimant would require eight months of rest due to the injuries and fractures suffered in the accident, but the tribunal has ignored the same and not awarded the suitable compensation under the head loss of income during laid up period and so also the tribunal has failed to award any compensation under the NC: 2024:KHC:2210 head loss of amenities.
For these reasons, he seeks to allow the appeal.
Consequently, to enhance the compensation.
5. Per contra, the learned counsel for the respondent No.2/insurance company contends that there is no error committed by the tribunal in awarding just and reasonable compensation.

The compensation is awarded based on the materials placed on record and in view of there being no cogent evidence with regard to proof of income, the tribunal has awarded just and reasonable compensation, which does not call for interference.
It is also contended by the learned counsel for the insurance company that the tribunal has awarded reasonable compensation and hence seeks for dismissal of the appeal.

sentences.text: I have heard the learned counsel for the appellant and learned counsel for respondent No.2/Insurance Company.
7. Perused the impugned judgment and award.

It is not in dispute that the accident occurred on 24.10.2016 between the motorcycle in which the claimant was proceeding as a pillion rider and the car - the offending vehicle, which dashed against the motorcycle of the claimant.
To substantiate NC: 2024:KHC:2210 these aspects, the claimant has produced Exs.P1 to P50.
Out of which, Exs.P1 to P7 are police records which are not disputed.

It is apparent that FIR is filed against the driver of the offending vehicle and so also the accident information report is also filed, which depicts that there is negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle, which has not been challenged.
In order to establish that injuries suffered and the magnitude of the same, Exs.P8 and P50 are produced which shows that the medical expenditures meted out by the claimant.

8. Now coming to the aspect of age, avocation and income of the claimant, it is stated that the claimant being aged 46 years, the appropriate multiplier for calculation would be '13', which is correctly applied by the tribunal and the same does not call for interference.

9. The tribunal has assessed the disability to an extent of 14% considering the evidence adduced by the Doctor-PW.2 and also taking into account the fact that Doctor-PW.2 has not assessed the disability to the whole body except to a particular limb.
I do not find any error in the said assessment made by NC: 2024:KHC:2210 the tribunal with regard to multiplier and disability assessed, the same is retained.
10. The income taken by the tribunal is Rs.9,000/- per month as notional income.
No documentary proof is produced before the tribunal to show the income.
However, the notional income chart of the Legal Services Authority prescribes the income of Rs.9,500/- for the accident of the year 2016.
Accordingly, income is taken as Rs.9,500/-.
Hence, the loss of future earning capacity due to disability would be Rs.2,07,480/- (Rs.9,500/- x 12 x 13 x 14%) as against Rs.1,96,560/- awarded by the tribunal.

11. Towards medical expenses, on the actual bills produced Rs.18,334/- is awarded by the tribunal,
which does not call for interference.
12. Towards conveyance, diet and attendant charges, Rs.15,000/- is awarded by the tribunal, which does not call for interference as the claimant was inpatient for two days.
13. Towards pain and suffering, Rs.50,000/- is awarded by the tribunal, which is also does not call for interference.
Towards loss of income during laid-up period, the tribunal has awarded Rs.27,000/- taking the income of Rs.9,000/- for three months.
Considering the evidence of the Doctor-PW.2, who has stated that eight months period would be required as bed rest.

This Court deems it appropriate to Sri Ananda vs Sri Manoj Kumar on 17 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/112474742/
4 calculate six months as laid-up period by considering two fractures and avocation of the claimant as Painter, which involves his leg movements and activities.

sentences.text: Therefore, the claimant would be entitled to Rs.57,000/- (Rs.9,500/- x 6) under the head loss of income during laid-up period.
15. It is seen that the tribunal has not awarded any amount towards loss of amenities.
This Court deems it appropriate to award Rs.50,000/- under this head.

16. In view of the above, the claimant would be entitled to a total compensation of Rs.3,97,814/- as against Rs.3,06,894/- as mentioned in the table below:

Accordingly, I pass the following:
